items.en: Hey look, there’s a sign on the wall.
items.zh: 嘿，看墙上有个标识。

items.en: It says, “No cameras or mobile phones!”
items.zh: 上面写着“禁止拍照或使用手机！”

items.en: Why do they have this sign at the entrance of the cinema?
items.zh: 电影院入口处为什么会有这个标识？

items.en: Well, I think it’s likely to prevent people from taking pictures or recording the movies.
items.zh: 嗯，我想大概是为了防止人们给电影拍照或录像。

items.en: Ah, that makes sense.
items.zh: 啊，有道理。

items.en: It’s important to respect the copyright laws that protect the movie industry.
items.zh: 尊重保护电影产业的版权法很重要。

items.en: That’s also why you can’t download certain movies online!
items.zh: 这也是为什么你不能在网上随意下载某些电影！

items.en: Have you noticed any other signs in public places?
items.zh: 你注意过公共场所的其他标识吗？

items.en: Yes, I remember seeing a sign in the library.
items.zh: 注意过，我记得在图书馆见过一个标识。

items.en: It said, “Silence is golden.”
items.zh: 上面写着“沉默是金”。

items.en: I’ve seen that one too.
items.zh: 那个我也见过。

items.en: It reminds us to be quiet and considerate of others.
items.zh: 它提醒我们要保持安静，体谅他人。

items.en: And what about in parks?
items.zh: 那公园里呢？

items.en: Have you seen any signs?
items.zh: 你见过什么标识吗？

items.en: Yes, I saw a sign at a national park that said, “Leave nothing but footprints.”
items.zh: 见过，我在一个国家公园见过一个标识，上面写着“只留脚印，不留其他”。

items.en: It encourages people to keep the park clean and not to leave any rubbish behind.
items.zh: 它鼓励人们保持公园清洁，不乱扔垃圾。

items.en: Signs in public places play an important role in promoting social rules and working for the common good.
items.zh: 公共场所的标识在倡导社会规则、维护公共利益方面发挥着重要作用。

items.en: Agreed.
items.zh: 同意。

items.en: Let’s always follow the rules and be good citizens.
items.zh: 我们一直遵守规则，做个好公民吧。

items.en: Now, let’s go enjoy the movie!
items.zh: 现在，我们去看电影吧！

items.en: Traffic laws are used to regulate the behaviour of drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists.
items.zh: 交通法规用来规范司机、行人和骑车人的行为。

items.en: Here are some key points about traffic laws.
items.zh: 以下是关于交通法规的几个要点。

items.en: Drivers must follow traffic laws on the street.
items.zh: 司机在街上必须遵守交通法规。

items.en: As a driver, you must therefore pay attention to traffic lights and other signals on the road.
items.zh: 因此，作为司机，你必须注意交通灯和路上的其他信号。

items.en: When you are planning to change lanes or make a turn, use your car’s turn signals.
items.zh: 打算变道或转弯时，要使用汽车转向灯。

items.en: Every driver and passenger in the car should wear a seat belt.
items.zh: 车上的每位司机和乘客都应系好安全带。

items.en: It can protect you and others in case of sudden stops or accidents.
items.zh: 万一突然刹车或发生事故，它能保护你和其他人。

items.en: As pedestrians, you should walk on the zebra crossings when crossing the street.
items.zh: 作为行人，过马路时应走斑马线。

items.en: You are only allowed to go when there is a green light and you must stop at red lights.
items.zh: 绿灯时才能通行，红灯时必须停下。

items.en: When you’re crossing the road, don’t check your phone.
items.zh: 过马路时，不要看手机。

items.en: When you are cycling on the road, keep to the right or left according to traffic laws.
items.zh: 在路上骑车时，要按交通法规靠右或靠左行驶。

items.en: Always wear a helmet when you ride an e-bike.
items.zh: 骑电动车时一定要戴头盔。

items.en: If you fall or get hit, the helmet will protect your head.
items.zh: 万一摔倒或被撞，头盔会保护你的头部。

items.en: When making a turn or a stop, use suitable hand signals to let others know what you are going to do.
items.zh: 转弯或停车时，要用合适的手势让别人知道你要做什么。

items.en: These laws can help keep us safe and prevent accidents.
items.zh: 这些法规能帮助我们保持安全，防止事故发生。

items.en: Spoken rules are said or written somewhere.
items.zh: 口头规则是被人说出来的，或写在某处的规则。

items.en: You might find spoken rules in school, public buildings, at home, or on the road.
items.zh: 你可能会在学校、公共建筑、家里或路上遇到口头规则。

items.en: Think of school rules.
items.zh: 想想学校的规则。

items.en: Are you allowed to run around and yell in the hallways?
items.zh: 你可以在走廊里到处乱跑、大喊大叫吗？

items.en: Are you allowed to insult others and cheat on tests?
items.zh: 你可以侮辱别人、考试作弊吗？

items.en: No!
items.zh: 不可以！

items.en: Think of rules in a public place, like a library or a park.
items.zh: 想想图书馆或公园这样的公共场所的规则。

items.en: Can you talk loudly in a library?
items.zh: 你能在图书馆里大声说话吗？

items.en: Can you climb on a park statue?
items.zh: 你能爬到公园的雕像上吗？

items.en: No!
items.zh: 不能！

items.en: At home, your parents might have clear rules like “no throwing basketballs in the house”.
items.zh: 在家里，父母可能会有明确的规定，比如“不许在屋里拍篮球”。

items.en: And on the road, you are required to follow traffic rules.
items.zh: 在路上，你必须遵守交通规则。

items.en: That can keep yourself and others safe.
items.zh: 这能让你和别人都保持安全。

items.en: Unspoken rules are mostly to do with respecting others.
items.zh: 不成文的规则主要与尊重他人有关。

items.en: This type of rule is different between countries and cultures!
items.zh: 这类规则在不同国家和文化中是不一样的！

items.en: You should recognise and follow the rules in your own country.
items.zh: 你应该了解并遵守自己国家的规则。

items.en: When you plan to visit another country, you should find out the differences to avoid being disrespectful.
items.zh: 当你打算去另一个国家时，应该先弄清那里的差异，以免冒犯别人。

items.en: For example, in some western countries, people don’t stand too close during a conversation.
items.zh: 例如，在一些西方国家，人们交谈时不会站得太近。

items.en: But, in many other countries, closeness is considered normal.
items.zh: 但在许多其他国家，靠得近被认为是正常的。

items.en: In some places, keeping more distance is seen as rude.
items.zh: 有些地方则把保持更远的距离看作不礼貌。

items.en: All these ways are acceptable.
items.zh: 这些做法都是可以接受的。

items.en: It depends on where in the world you are!
items.zh: 这取决于你身在世界何处！

items.en: “Stop it!” says Jenny, stepping away from Danny.
items.zh: “住手！”珍妮说着，从丹尼身边退开。

items.en: “I have asked you to stop pulling my hair three times already!”
items.zh: “我已经让你别拽我头发，都说过三次了！”

items.en: “I’m just playing,” laughs Danny.
items.zh: “我只是闹着玩，”丹尼笑着说。

items.en: Just then, Mr Dino walks over.
items.zh: 就在这时，迪诺老师走了过来。

items.en: He asks Jenny if everything is okay.
items.zh: 他问珍妮一切是否还好。

items.en: Jenny shakes her head and looks away, hiding her hair under her hood.
items.zh: 珍妮摇摇头，把目光移开，把头发藏进兜帽里。

items.en: “Danny, your friend is setting a boundary.
items.zh: “丹尼，你的朋友在划定边界。

items.en: You need to respect it!” warns Mr Dino.
items.zh: 你必须尊重它！”迪诺老师警告说。

items.en: “A what?” says Danny.
items.zh: “什么？”丹尼说。

items.en: “A boundary,” says Mr Dino.
items.zh: “边界，”迪诺老师说。

items.en: He goes on to explain, “A boundary is a rule we set for ourselves.
items.zh: 他接着解释：“边界是我们为自己定下的规则。

items.en: It helps us feel safe and respected.
items.zh: 它让我们感到安全和被尊重。

items.en: Do you remember when Uncle Dino wanted to give you a hug, but you didn’t want one?
items.zh: 你还记得迪诺叔叔想抱你，但你不想让他抱吗？

items.en: You told him, ‘Not this time.’
items.zh: 你告诉他：‘这次不行。’

items.en: You set a personal boundary.
items.zh: 你就设定了一个个人边界。

items.en: Jenny is doing the same thing.”
items.zh: 珍妮现在做的也是一样。”

items.en: Mr Dino adds, “Listening to others’ boundaries shows respect and makes them feel they can trust you.
items.zh: 迪诺老师补充说：“倾听别人的边界，是尊重他们，也能让他们觉得可以信任你。

items.en: Boundaries teach you to notice when someone might be dangerous.”
items.zh: 边界能教你察觉某人是否可能带来危险。”

items.en: Danny nods and says, “I get it.”
items.zh: 丹尼点点头说：“我明白了。”

items.en: Then, he turns to Jenny, “I was not paying attention to your feelings.
items.zh: 然后，他转向珍妮：“我之前没有顾及你的感受。

items.en: I am so sorry for what I did!”
items.zh: 我为自己的行为感到非常抱歉！”

items.en: “That’s okay, Danny,” smiles Jenny.
items.zh: “没关系，丹尼，”珍妮笑着说。

items.en: “Just keep working on it!”
items.zh: “继续努力就好！”

items.en: Following public rules and regulations is an important part of living in a society.
items.zh: 遵守公共规则和规定是社会生活的重要组成部分。

items.en: What happens when people don’t follow public rules?
items.zh: 如果人们不遵守公共规则，会发生什么呢？

items.en: Here are some cases.
items.zh: 下面就是几个例子。

items.en: Case 1: Cutting in line
items.zh: 案例一：插队

items.en: Cutting in line is often considered an annoying behaviour that creates a sense of impatience.
items.zh: 插队通常被认为是一种令人讨厌的行为，会让人不耐烦。

items.en: It breaks social fairness and is rude.
items.zh: 它破坏了社会公平，也很不礼貌。

items.en: It can lead to arguments and even fights.
items.zh: 它可能导致争吵，甚至打架。

items.en: Case 2: Spreading rumours
items.zh: 案例二：散布谣言

items.en: Have you ever met someone who spreads rumours?
items.zh: 你遇到过散布谣言的人吗？

items.en: Whether in person or on the internet, spreading false or negative information is disrespectful to others or even illegal.
items.zh: 无论是当面还是在网上，散布虚假或负面信息都是对别人的不尊重，甚至可能违法。

items.en: This behaviour can damage other’s reputation.
items.zh: 这种行为会损害别人的名誉。

items.en: We should never spread rumours without finding out the truth.
items.zh: 在弄清真相之前，我们绝不应散布谣言。

items.en: It only causes trouble.
items.zh: 它只会带来麻烦。

items.en: Case 3: Littering
items.zh: 案例三：乱扔垃圾

items.en: Littering is a very bad behaviour.
items.zh: 乱扔垃圾是一种非常不好的行为。

items.en: When people litter, not only the environment but also the health and safety of others are affected.
items.zh: 人们乱扔垃圾时，受影响的不只是环境，还有他人的健康与安全。

items.en: It is everyone’s responsibility to protect the planet.
items.zh: 保护地球是每个人的责任。

items.en: Don’t be the one to make a mess!
items.zh: 别做那个把环境弄得一团糟的人！

items.en: Following public rules protects the people and the world around us.
items.zh: 遵守公共规则保护着我们身边的人和周围的世界。

items.en: It’s important for us to understand and keep the rules of our society.
items.zh: 理解并遵守社会规则对我们很重要。

items.en: You may want to remember these strange laws next time you’re travelling to avoid fines!
items.zh: 下次旅行时，你也许该记住这些奇怪的法律，以免被罚款！

items.en: Don’t eat on church steps in Italy.
items.zh: 在意大利，不要坐在教堂台阶上吃东西。

items.en: Be careful where you enjoy a relaxing lunch or drink in Italy.
items.zh: 在意大利，吃一顿悠闲的午餐或喝点东西时，要注意地点。

items.en: It’s an offense in Florence to eat or drink on church steps or within a church yard.
items.zh: 在佛罗伦萨，在教堂台阶上或教堂院子里吃喝是违法的。

items.en: The same law applies to eating near public buildings or institutions.
items.zh: 同样的法律也适用于在公共建筑或机构附近吃东西。

items.en: Find other places to avoid the fine.
items.zh: 换个地方吧，免得被罚款。

items.en: Watch your camera in Kazakhstan.
items.zh: 在哈萨克斯坦，看好你的相机。

items.en: Want to take a picture of your family in the airport before you board the plane?
items.zh: 想在登机前在机场给家人拍张照吗？

items.en: In Kazakhstan, it’s against the law.
items.zh: 在哈萨克斯坦，这是违法的。

items.en: Photographing in and around airports is not allowed, and taking pictures of military and official buildings is not allowed either.
items.zh: 机场内及周边禁止拍照，军事建筑和官方建筑也不允许拍照。

items.en: Feed the pigeons and you’ll break the law in San Francisco.
items.zh: 在旧金山喂鸽子，你就违法了。

items.en: You’re not allowed to feed pigeons on the streets of San Francisco.
items.zh: 旧金山街头不允许喂鸽子。

items.en: The city doesn’t like the birds because they spread diseases and damage properties.
items.zh: 这座城市不喜欢这些鸟，因为它们传播疾病、损坏财物。

items.en: If you’re seen giving food to San Francisco’s pigeons, you could be punished with a fine.
items.zh: 如果被发现给旧金山的鸽子喂食，你可能会被罚款。

items.en: Pack a breathalyzer in France.
items.zh: 在法国，随车带上酒精测试仪。

items.en: In France, drivers must carry a small breathalyzer in their vehicle.
items.zh: 在法国，司机必须在车里带一个小型酒精测试仪。

items.en: If you’re caught without one in your car, you may be fined.
items.zh: 如果在车里被查到没带，你可能会被罚款。

items.en: So next time you are in France, don’t forget to have a breathalyzer in the car with you.
items.zh: 所以下次去法国，别忘了在车里放一个酒精测试仪。
